To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
having more WMH in older age is independently associated with lower cognitive function after accounting for prior cognitive ability, and that early-life IQ influences later life WMH.

having more WMH in later age was associated independently with lower late life cognitive ability, after taking into account prior IQ and other factors, and that lower IQ in youth was also independently associated with more WMH in older age.

(a) having more white matter hyperintensity (WMH), a marker of brain aging, is significantly associated with having lower cognitive ability, even after accounting for prior cognitive ability; (b) having more WMH also predicts having higher blood pressure and being hypertensive; and (c) having lower intelligence in childhood predicts greater white matter damage in older adulthood.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of early life IQ on the relationship between brain damage with aging and late life cognitive function.
the association between brain white matter damage and cognitive ability in aging, and how childhood intelligence influences these relationships.
how brain damage in later life is associated with cognitive impairment, and how early-life IQ may affect brain damage in later years.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the brain white matter damage in the elderly is significantly associated with the lower cognitive ability after accounting for prior cognitive ability, age 10 IQ.
the relationship between WMH and cognitive impairment is independent of IQ.
the relationship between cognitive ability in childhood and in later life is mediated by white matter hyperintensity load.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
WMH load is significantly associated with late life cognitive ability, independent of prior ability, after accounting also for age 11IQ and hypertension.
WMH is a significant predictor of lower cognitive ability in late life, after accounting for age 1 IQ and that WMH is also associated independently with both lower IQ at age 11 and hypertension.

The main takeaway from our work is that
childhood IQ is an important factor to consider in studies of brain aging and cognitive impairment.
the brain is not a static organ.
childhood IQ is a strong predictor of late life cognition.
